Assistant: The store slot is already published by the actor at kernel construction and republished on reset, so the primitive can reuse that D4 ownership model. The design should move access into `ActionContext`/execution context, not introduce a second store owner or a native-visible query API. [...] Core design: make `ActionContext` the action-runtime capability bag, pass it into `ActionModule::execute`, and expose a bounded Rust-only local store reader. That replaces the PR #2131 per-action `EventStoreSlot` capture pattern without adding a native-visible query API or relay-fetch path. [...] 
Assistant: The existing store abstraction already gives us the right bounded query primitive. I’m going to make `ActionContext` a thin wrapper over either a published `EventStoreSlot` or a direct `Arc<dyn EventStore>`, with explicit “store unavailable” and “limit exceeded” errors. [...] Assistant: The runtime dispatch paths now build store-backed contexts. I’m doing the mechanical trait migration next: every existing action module gets `_ctx: &ActionContext` unless it actually reads the store.
 [...] Assistant: Both nextest jobs point at scaffold compilation, not runtime behavior of the new primitive: the workspace job fails `nmp-cli::init`, and the serial job fails the `nmp-testing` fresh-scaffold gate. I’m extracting the compiler diagnostics next; that will tell us whether this is just stale generated template code. [...] 1. Update the scaffold generator/templates to include `&ActionContext` in generated `execute`.
